paired_preferences.reason: Both are coherent professional studios across themes and widths. S03 carries its distinctive condensed serif, compass motif and numbered dossier sections more deeply into the working product, exposes the complete desktop note form within the captured dialog, and gives mobile project rows more immediate space. S05 has an excellent explicit-date timeline and attractive broader serif, but its repeated mobile header/breadcrumb/intro stack delays core work and its desktop note save action is below the captured fold. This preference concerns visible craft and task presentation, not untested functionality.

Both preserve the notebook relationship, readable source hierarchy, clear selection, retry and source-specific note feedback. S02's expanded desktop view adds a useful contents rail, taller note field and explicit Expand/Compact labels, but the captured expansion briefly crops that rail and its phone compact state exposes little prose. S07 keeps a simpler, consistent note placement and exposes more summary on the phone, but its permanent bottom form reduces desktop reading space and its top mode action is icon-only. These visible tradeoffs do not support a clear overall preference; continuous motion and behavioral correctness were not evaluated.

Both are mature and consistent across themes, with readable records and well-integrated detail surfaces. S10 has a more immediately useful workload overview with upcoming deadlines, richer project cards, and a desktop/tablet timeline that makes overlapping fieldwork visible; its mobile schedule also reaches more records within the initial screen. S09's comparative project register is more efficient for scanning many project attributes, and its monthly agenda is clear, so the preference is weak. The decision concerns visible work presentation and identity, not untested business behavior.

Both support a mature populated research journey with clear source reading, cited answers, follow-up writing and recoverable error presentation. S04 has a more distinctive editorial identity, exposes all three source titles in the phone conversation and supplies visible previous/next controls inside the reader. S08 has especially comfortable larger body text and a clear retained-draft waiting message, so the preference is weak. It rests on visible reading/navigation presentation, not untested functionality or continuous animation.

Both closely preserve the notebook identity, provide explicit mode/source controls, and communicate loading, retained drafts, retry and saved notes clearly. S11 uses its desktop/tablet reading space more effectively: the compact capture exposes the complete summary, the expanded capture shows the full quotation, and Read full text stays beside the summary heading at every reviewed width. S12 has a stronger boxed summary and more emphatic selected-source treatment, so the preference is weak. Motion smoothness and actual persistence were not assessed.

Both are coherent, mature research frontends with clear source-before-answer hierarchy, useful desktop outlines, readable full source notes, persistent writing and explicit waiting/failure states. S01 exposes all three source titles on the phone and clearly separates conversation name from the user question, but its compact cards lose publisher context and its long outline repeats indistinguishable labels. S06 gives primary actions and reader navigation stronger labels, retains publisher context and numbers outline entries, but puts phone sources offscreen and keeps an empty outline heading during waiting/failure. These visible tradeoffs do not justify a clear overall preference; functionality and continuous motion remain untested.

overall_limitations: Independent model visual judgments, not human-user study results. Review remained anonymous and followed the six-pair order supplied to R2; no instruction-treatment identity was inferred.

Actual image coverage: 279 unique supplied images, comprising 156 individual stable captures, 36 supplemental captures, 60 individual ordered temporal samples, 24 stable/temporal overview sheets, and all three Vane author benchmark images. Every output and every matched pair is represented.

All T1 stable views were inspected as original images: conversation and source reader at 1440, 900 and 390 pixels in both themes, plus every supplied pending, error and long-content capture. T2 originals covered all four working views at 1440 initial theme, 900 alternate theme, and 390 in both themes; the remaining T2 stable theme/width combinations were surveyed in the stable overview sheets rather than individually at full size.

For T3, compact, expanded and second-source views at all three widths, desktop and phone notebook views, and all error/note supplemental captures were inspected as originals. The 900-pixel notebook was surveyed in the overview sheet only. Margin evidence supplied one theme; no unavailable theme is inferred.

Continuous natural-motion quality is unassessed: no sequence.webm was watched. Temporal overview sheets and selected original ordered samples establish captured states, geometry and visible continuity only, not physical-device behavior, frame rate, exact perceptual timing, easing quality or interruption correctness.

Screenshot evidence does not prove functional completeness, keyboard and screen-reader behavior, focus restoration, reduced-motion operation, source request races, persistence, attachments, all source changes, arbitrary long-content scrolling or mobile software-keyboard behavior. Visible controls and state messages were evaluated without claiming their underlying behavior.

Vane maturity comparison uses only the three supplied author screenshots and their declared local frontend comparison scope. No commercial backend, live research quality or service parity is inferred.

No source code, participant handovers, execution logs, performance/functional-test results, version assignments, other reviewers' records, personal context or outside-workspace material was inspected. No supplied evidence was modified. Contrast and legibility judgments are visual, without a numerical accessibility audit or alternate-device rendering tests.

All six dimensions have observable visual evidence, so none is null; the states dimension is limited to visible communication and sampled continuity. No dimensions were summed or converted into a total or percentage.
